timecoded_text_to_speech.text: I'm Lauren, so today we have rubber with us. I'm going to ask several questions. So I know that you have been traveling globally, meeting like, where's customers and regulator.
What might be something that maybe isn't in the press that you like as to know?
As part of our operations, expanding Luca globally, have visited approaching 20 countries this year alone.

And I'm meeting with our customers with various regulators around the world. And I'd say some of the biggest takeaways that I'm noticing that maybe isn't as apparent in the press as there's a ton of effort going into the mature adoption of tokenized assets, whether it's

crypto or now tokenizing traditional assets. We're seeing a lot of different frameworks and businesses that are getting ready to launch, which is very exciting to see even though maybe in in the US, we're seeing less certainty.
But I'd say it's not slowing down the rest of the world.
So Luca was the first company in the crypto industry to like, obtain that SOC one report in 2018. And you're now using some more globally recognized freaks frameworks.
So like, how do you see what's your fault here and how does that relate to the data business?
Sure. Yeah. So we're in 2018, the AICPA SOC one type two was our first one. We were the first in the industry to obtain that, which really for anyone that's not familiar.
It's all about processing integrity and data completeness and making sure that our products do that. So if we have software, making sure gain loss computations are accurate and the data is complete.
We've since added on a SOC two and also ISO certifications. We have our look of prime products certification of adherence from IOSCO under their financial principles for benchmarks.

And so, and we'll continue to get all of those different things that our customers need to help them trust us. I'd say that they're, they're even more important when we're dealing with crypto assets because this ecosystem uses a lot more data and a lot more technology than traditional markets to.

And it's a new technology that's very innovative. So we need to think about risk in some new ways, but still need to think about risks. So it's the same old frameworks, but we're applying them to new new technology risks that now exist today.

And that's been a big differentiator of Lucas from the beginning. So we'll continue to get those to help customers trust us. And it's really built into our organizations DNA is thinking about risk management first when we're building all of these products.

Well, yeah, I heard that Lucas recently acquired a confirm and adding like on trim capability to support ML and compliant use the cases. So like, what do you see how this does fit into the other software or like data offerings?
Yeah, so we started off managing data for our customers and we built data products internally for our own internal use honestly to make the software work.
So whether they're pricing products or other standardization related products like our our local reference data product.
Now today fast forward we're we've been offering all of those products for several years to a lot of the biggest institutions in the world both crypto native and traditional.
Once you have your your back office and your portfolio management or your books and records organized and you're auditable.
You additionally need to manage counter party risk. You need to make sure that you're complying with money laundering rules and other compliance use cases.
So acquiring coin firm and all of their products was a natural opportunity for Luca as it's really just another capability that all of our existing customers need.
So we're very excited to be offering it in conjunction with our services and we are now the only company in the world that can offer software to manage data transaction data.

The data products as standalone products and also compliance and AML products all under under one house which has become very important particularly recently when when companies are cost cutting a bit more than usual just due to the economic conditions and they're looking to consolidate vendors or streamline legal reviews vendor risk reviews and things like that.
So very excited to have a part of them this year.
Thank you Robert for sharing all those information with us. Yeah and thank you for having us today.

INTERVIEW 🎙️ Robert Materazzi, CEO, Lukka

You have been traveling globally, meeting customers and regulators, what might be something that isn't in the press that you would like us to know as part of your operations expanding Lukka?
❖ "Globally I visited, approaching 20 countries this year alone and meeting with our customers, with various regulators around the world. I'd say some of the biggest takeaways that I'm noticing that maybe isn't as apparent in the press is that there's a ton of effort going into the mature adoption of tokenized assets whether it's crypto or now tokenizing traditional assets. We're seeing a lot of different frameworks and businesses that are getting ready to launch which is very exciting to see, even though maybe in the U.S. we're seeing less certainty. But I'd say, it's not slowing down the rest of the world." 

Lukka was the first company serving the crypto industry to perform an AICPA SOC 1 Type II audit in 2018 and you're now using some more globally recognized frameworks.  What are your thoughts, how does that relate to the data business?
❖ In 2018 AICPA SOC 1type II was our first one. We were the first one the industry to obtain it which really for anyone that's not familiar it's all about processing integrity and data completeness and making sure that our products do that. So, if we have software, making sure gain-loss computations are accurate and the data is complete. We've since added on SOC 2 and also ISO/IEC certification, we have our Lukka Prime products, a certification of adherence from AICPA under their financial principles for benchmarks and we'll continue to get all of those different things that our customers need to help them trust us. I'd say that they're even more important when we're dealing with crypto assets because this ecosystem uses a lot more data and a lot more technology than traditional markets do, and it's a new technology that's very innovative. So we need to think about risk in some new ways but still need to think about risk. So, it's the same old frameworks but we're applying them to new technology risks that now exist today and that's been a big differentiator of Lukka from the beginning. So we'll continue to get those to help customers trust us and it's really built into our organization's DNA.  It is thinking about risk management first when we're building all of these products."

Lukka has recently acquired Coinfirm and adding their capability to support AML and compliant user cases. What do you see, how does this fit into the other software data offerings? 
❖ "We started off managing data for our customers and we built data products internally for our own internal use to make the software work. So whether they're pricing products or other standardization related products like our Lukka reference data product. Now today fast-forward, we've been offering all those products for several years to a lot of the biggest institutions in the world, both crypto native and traditional. Once you have your back office and your portfolio management or your books and records organized and you're auditable, you additionally need to manage counterparty risk. You need to make sure that you're complying with money laundering rules and other compliance use cases. Acquiring Coinfirm and all of their products was a natural   for Lukka as it's really just another capability that all of our existing customers need. We're very excited to be offering it in conjunction with our services and we are now the only company in the world that can offer software to manage data transaction data, the data products as standalone products, and also compliance and AML products, all under one house which has become very important. In particular recently, when companies are cost-cutting a bit more than usual due to the economic conditions and they're looking to consolidate vendors or streamline legal reviews vendor risk reviews. So, I am very excited to have acquired them this year."
